EASTERN MEDITERRANEAN SEA
THE HELLENIC NAVY IN COORDINATION WITH THE HELLENIC COAST
GUARD WILL CONDUCT A NAVAL COOPERATION AND GUIDANCE FOR
SHIPPING (NCAGS) EXERCISE UNDER THE NAME ''MINOAS 2026''
FROM 130500 UTC OCTOBER 26 UNTIL 161200 UTC OCTOBER 26.
THE NCAGS AREA IS DEFINED AS THE HIGH SEAS OF THE
AEGEAN SEA, THE IONIAN SEA AND SEA OF KASTELORIZO.
NCAGS PROCEDURES WILL BE USED IN ORDER TO INTERACT
WITH MERCHANT SHIPPING DURING THE SPECIFIED EXERCISE PERIOD.
MERCHANT SHIPPING AND MERCHANT VESSELS
(INCLUDING FISHING VESSELS GREATER THAN 300GRT) ARE KINDLY
REQUESTED TO COOPERATE WITH THE NCAGS COORDINATION CENTRE
(NCC)LOCATED AT HELLENIC COAST GUARD HQ IN PIRAEUS,
ON A NO COST-NO DELAY VOLUNTARY BASIS.
MERCHANT VESSELS ARE ENCOURAGED TO COMMUNICATE DIRECTLY
WITH NCC PRIOR ENTERING OR SAILING OUT OF THE SPECIFIED NCAGS
AREA BY PHONE OR BY TRANSMITTING A NON FORMATTED TEXT
(VIA EMAIL), INFORMING OF THEIR WILL TO PARTICIPATE IN THE EXERCISE.
POINT OF CONTACT DURING THE EXERCISE: NCAGS COORDINATION CENTRE,
EMAIL: HELLENICNCAGS(AT)NAVY.MIL.GR (ALL LOWERCASE)
PHONE NO: +302131371031
CANCEL THIS MSG 161300 UTC OCT 26

records.original:
PERSIAN GULF
STRAIT OF HORMUZ
CHARTS BA 2837, 2851, 2858, 2888, 3172, 3174, OM1219
AND OM1218
SULTANATE OF OMAN HAS ISSUED FOLLOWING ADVISORY
1. THE SULTANATE OF OMAN BASED ON ITS RESPONSIBILITIES TOWARD THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ, AND ITS IMPORTANCE TO THE GLOBAL ECONOMY, AND IN ACCORDANCE TO ITS CONTINUED COMMITMENT TO THE INTERNATIONAL LAW AND THE LAW OF THE SEA TO ENSURE FREEDOM OF NAVIGATION IN THE STRAIT WITHOUT IMPOSING ANY TOLLS, IN LINE WITH THE OUTCOMES AND EFFORTS REACHED BY THE UNITED STATES AND ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN.
2. THE SULTANATE OF OMAN HAS WORKED IN COORDINATION WITH THE INTERNATIONAL MARITIME ORGANIZATION (IMO) TO PROVIDE
ALL VESSELS WITH THE OPTION OF A TEMPORARY MARITIME  CORRIDOR DEFINED BY THE COORDINATES LISTED BELOW.
3. THE SAFETY OF NAVIGATION REMAINS THE PARAMOUNT CONSIDERATION.GIVEN THE ELEVATED RISK OF COLLISION IN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT,
A GRADUAL AND CONTROLLED EVACUATION OF VESSEL TRAFFIC IS REQUIRED.
4. TO MITIGATE THESE RISKS, THE IMO HAS DEVELOPED A PHASED APPROACH BASED ON GROUPS OF VESSELS WITH THE FULL COORDINATION
OF THE OMANI AUTHORITIES.
5. CURRENT REPORTS INDICATE THAT THE TSS IS NOT SAFE FOR USE AT THIS TIME. BASED ON AVAILABLE INFORMATION FROM THE IMO, TWO TEMPORARY ROUTES MAY BE UTILIZED BY VESSELS DEPARTING THROUGH THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ: ONE SOUTH OF THE EXISTING TRAFFIC SEPARATION SCHEME (TSS) AND ONE TO THE NORTH.
6. VESSELS INCLUDED IN THE DESIGNATED GROUPS WILL BE CONTACTED INDIVIDUALLY AND PROVIDED WITH FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING THEIR DEPARTURE BY RELEVANT PARTIES COORDINATED BY THE IMO.
7. INSTRUCTIONS FOR TRANSIT: VESSELS WILL BE CONTACTED INDIVIDUALLY AND ADVISED OF THEIR ALLOCATED TRANSIT DAY BY THE PARTIES COORDINATED BY IMO.
8. UPON RECEIPT OF THIS INFORMATION, VESSELS MAY PROCEED TO THE DESIGNATED WAITING AREA WITHIN INTERNATIONAL WATERS, WITHIN A 3 NM RADIUS OF POSITION 26-16.17N/055-46.52E.
9. UPON ARRIVAL AT THE DESIGNATED WAITING AREA, VESSELS  SHALL CONTACT THE RELEVANT COASTAL STATE OF THEIR SELECTED ROUTE TO CONFIRM THAT TRAFFIC CONDITIONS PERMIT THEM TO PROCEED. FOR THE SULTANATE OF OMAN, VESSELS SHALL ALSO RE-CONTACT RADIO
STATION "A4N" ON VHF CH. 16 WHEN 1 NM FROM THE FIRST WAYPOINT BELOW.
FOR THE SULTANATE OF OMAN, THE ROUTES THAT HAVE BEEN AUTHORIZED FOR EASTBOUND TRANSIT ONLY ARE AS FOLLOWS:
A. 26-02.72N 056-00.68E
B. 26-22.56N 056-16.93E
C. 26-24.35N 056-23.00E
D. 26-24.75N 056-31.11E
E. 26-22.10N 056-33.42E
F. 26-00.00N 056-33.30E
10. EACH SHIPOWNER AND MASTER REMAINS RESPONSIBLE FOR CONDUCTING AN INDEPENDENT RISK ASSESSMENT PRIOR TO VOYAGE.
11. VESSELS SHALL ENSURE AIS IS ON WHILE TRANSITING, LRIT, WHERE APPLICABLE, SHOULD ALSO BE USED. VESSELS SHALL COMPLY WITH ALL
INSTRUCTIONS ISSUED BY COASTAL STATES VIA VHF.
12. IMO WILL REPORT DAILY ON THE NUMBER OF VESSELS SAFELY DEPARTING THE REGION.
13. VESSEL TRAFFIC MAY BE TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED FOR SAFETY OR SECURITY PURPOSES, INCLUDING DECONFLICTION WITH NAVAL VESSELS.
14. VESSELS SHOULD REPORT ANY DANGER TO NAVIGATION TO THE OMAN MARITIME SECURITY CENTRE AT (00968 91400430/OMSC@MOD.GOV.OM).
15. FURTHER INFORMATION ON EMERGENCY TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT MEASURES WILL BE ISSUED BY RELEVANT PARTIES COORDINATED BY THE IMO AND THE COASTAL STATES OF THE REGION.
